# 1 Enoch Chapter 89 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Book of Dreams — Animal Apocalypse

---

**1** One of those four [an archangel] went to the white bull [Noah] and gave him a secret message. Without being frightened, he changed into a man, built a vessel, and lived in it. Three other bulls [Shem, Ham, Japheth] lived with him in the vessel, and they were sealed inside.

**2** I looked up at heaven and saw a great roof with seven torrents of water pouring down from it, all flowing into an enclosure [the earth].

**3** Then I saw fountains open across the surface of that great enclosure. The water began to swell and rise over the surface until the whole enclosure was submerged.

**4** Water, darkness, and mist grew heavier. I watched the water rise higher and higher until it crested the rim of the enclosure and spilled out across the earth.

**5** All the animals in the enclosure gathered together — and I watched them sink down, swallowed up and destroyed by the water.

**6** But the vessel floated on top of the water while all the cattle, elephants, camels, and donkeys — and all the animals — sank to the bottom, unable to escape, perishing in the deep.

**7** I watched until the water-torrents were turned off from the great roof and the chasms of the earth were filled. New abysses opened up.

**8** The water drained into them until the earth reappeared. The vessel settled on dry ground. The darkness lifted and light returned.

**9** The white bull who had become a man came out of the vessel [Noah emerges], and the three bulls with him [his three sons]. One of those three was white like Noah [Shem], one was red as blood [Japheth], and one was black [Ham]. The first white bull [Noah] departed from them.

**10** They began to produce animals of all kinds — lions, tigers, wolves, dogs, hyenas, wild boars, foxes, squirrels, swine, falcons, vultures, kites, eagles, and ravens [the nations of the world born from Noah's sons]. And among these a white bull was born [Abraham].

**11** The animals began attacking each other. But the white bull born among them fathered a wild donkey [Ishmael] and another white bull [Isaac], and the wild donkeys multiplied.

**12** That white bull [Isaac] fathered a black wild boar [Esau] and a white sheep [Jacob/Israel]. The boar fathered many boars [Edomites], but that sheep [Jacob] fathered twelve sheep [the twelve tribes of Israel].

**13** When those twelve sheep grew up, they handed one of them over to the donkeys [Joseph sold to Ishmaelites], and the donkeys handed that sheep over to the wolves [sold to Egypt]. That sheep grew up among the wolves [Joseph in Egypt].

**14** The Lord brought the other eleven sheep to live with it among the wolves [Israel's descent into Egypt]. They multiplied greatly.

**15** The wolves grew afraid of them and called out to their pack. The wolves made war on the eleven sheep, killing some; but the others escaped and cried out to their Lord [Israel's oppression in Egypt].

**16** A sheep that had escaped the wolves [Moses] fled to the wild donkeys. I watched the sheep cry out to their Lord with everything in them, until the Lord of the sheep [God] came down from his high dwelling and tended them himself.

**17** He called that escaped sheep [Moses] and spoke with it about the wolves — it was to warn the wolves to stop harming the sheep.

**18** The sheep [Moses] went to the wolves [Pharaoh's court] as the Lord commanded. Another sheep [Aaron] met it and went with it, and together the two entered the assembly of the wolves and warned them to leave the sheep alone.

**19** But I watched the wolves crush the sheep with all their power. The sheep cried out.

**20** The Lord came to the sheep and they began to strike the wolves [the plagues]. The wolves wailed; the sheep fell silent and stopped crying.

**21** I watched as the sheep left the wolves. But the wolves' eyes were blinded, and they chased after the sheep with full force [Pharaoh's army pursues Israel].

**22** The Lord of the sheep led them — his face blazing, glorious, and terrifying.

**23** The wolves chased the sheep until they reached a sea [the Red Sea].

**24** The sea split open — water on both sides — and their Lord led them forward, placing himself between the sheep and the wolves.

**25** The wolves, not yet seeing the sheep clearly, drove into the middle of the sea, running after them.

**26** When they saw the Lord of the sheep, they tried to flee — but the sea closed back to its original form. The water swelled and rose and swallowed the wolves [the drowning of Pharaoh's army].

**27** I watched until every wolf pursuing the sheep had perished and drowned.

**28** The sheep came out of the water and entered a wilderness with no water, no grass [Sinai desert]. Their eyes began to open. I watched the Lord of the sheep feeding them — giving them water and grass — and that leading sheep [Moses] guided them.

**29** That sheep [Moses] climbed to the summit of a great rock [Sinai], and the Lord of the sheep sent him to them [the giving of the Law].

**30** Then the Lord of the sheep appeared before them — towering, terrible, and majestic. All the sheep saw him and were afraid.

**31** They trembled and cried to their leading sheep: "We cannot stand before our Lord or look at him."

**32** The leading sheep [Moses] climbed back to the summit of the rock. But the sheep began to go blind and wander from the path he had shown them [the golden calf]. Their leader knew nothing of it.

**33** The Lord of the sheep was furious with them. The leading sheep [Moses] discovered it, came down from the summit, found the flock mostly blinded and fallen away.

**34** When they saw him, they shook with fear and wanted to go back to their fold.

**35** The leading sheep gathered some other sheep and went to those who had gone astray and began to kill them [Moses's execution of the idolaters]. The rebellious sheep were terrified, and the fallen ones were brought back to their fold.

**36** I watched in the vision as that sheep [Moses] became a man and built a house for the Lord of the sheep [the Tabernacle] and placed all the sheep inside.

**37** I watched as the sheep that had met the first leader [Aaron] fell asleep [died]. And all the great sheep died, and smaller ones took their place. They came to a pasture and approached a river [entry into Canaan/Jordan River].

**38** Then their leader — the sheep who had become a man [Moses] — withdrew from them and fell asleep [died]. All the sheep searched for him and wept bitterly.

**39** I watched them stop weeping and cross the river [crossing the Jordan]. Two sheep arose as their new leaders [Joshua and Caleb] in place of those who had died.

**40** I watched the sheep enter a beautiful, pleasant, and glorious land [Canaan]. They were satisfied, and the house [the Tabernacle/Tent of Meeting] stood among them in that pleasant land.

**41** But their eyes kept opening and closing [cycles of faithfulness and apostasy in Judges], until another sheep arose [a judge] and led them back each time, and their eyes were opened.

**42** Dogs, foxes, and wild boars began to devour those sheep [the Philistines and other enemies] until the Lord of the sheep raised a ram from among them to lead them [Saul/David].

**43** That ram attacked the dogs, foxes, and wild boars on every side and destroyed them all.

**44** But the sheep whose eyes had been opened watched as that ram [Saul] left behind his glory and started to attack the very sheep he led, trampling them and behaving shamefully.

**45** So the Lord of the sheep sent a lamb to another lamb [Samuel to David] and raised it to become the new ram and leader — in place of the ram that had abandoned its glory.

**46** He went to the lamb alone and spoke with it and elevated it to be a ram — the prince and leader of the sheep. All the while the dogs were still attacking the sheep.

**47** The first ram [Saul] pursued the second [David], and the second fled. Then I watched the dogs bring down the first ram [Saul's death].

**48** The second ram [David] arose and led the young sheep. The sheep grew and multiplied. All the dogs, foxes, and wild boars fled before him. The ram destroyed the wild beasts and they no longer had any power over the sheep or stole from them.

**49** That ram [David] fathered many sheep and fell asleep [died]. A little sheep [Solomon] became ram and ruler in his place.

**50** The house [the Temple] became great and wide — it was built for the sheep. A tall, lofty tower was built on top of the house for the Lord of the sheep [Solomon's Temple]. The house was low but the tower rose high, and the Lord of the sheep stood on the tower. They offered him a full table [the sacrificial system of the Temple].

**51** But then I saw the sheep go astray again — wandering in every direction, abandoning their house. The Lord of the sheep sent some of the sheep to warn them [the prophets], but the sheep began to kill them.

**52** One of those sent [Elijah? Jeremiah?] escaped and was not killed. He ran out and called to the sheep in anguish. They tried to kill him too, but the Lord of the sheep rescued him and brought him to me [the prophet taken to safety/Enoch].

**53** And the Lord sent many other sheep to testify to them and mourn over them [the succession of prophets].

**54** Then I saw that when they abandoned the Lord's house and tower, they fell away completely. Their eyes went blind. I watched the Lord of the sheep bring terrible destruction among them — until the sheep themselves invited the destruction and betrayed his place [the apostasy preceding the exile].

**55** He gave them over to lions, tigers, wolves, hyenas, foxes, and all the wild beasts [the imperial powers — Assyria, Babylon]. The wild beasts tore the sheep apart.

**56** I saw him abandon their house and tower and hand them all over to the lions — to tear apart and devour — and to all the wild beasts.

**57** I cried out with all my strength to the Lord of the sheep. Then I saw him walk away from them [the Shekinah departing from the Temple].

**58** The sheep were eaten by the dogs, burned by the wolves, and scattered across the heights.

**59** I saw that the tower and house were flooded with water. I could no longer see the Lord of the sheep standing there in the glory of that tower. The sheep wandered away, were carried off, and I watched them descend into a dark and terrible place [the exile to Babylon].

**60** And the sheep were handed over — seventy shepherds [angelic rulers of the nations] were assigned to pasture them. The Shepherd said to those seventy shepherds: "Each of you is to pasture these sheep from now on. Do exactly what I command you."

**61** He handed the sheep over to them. Then he called another [a recording angel] and told him: "Watch and record everything those shepherds do to these sheep — they will destroy more than I have commanded.

**62** Record every excess and every act of destruction by the shepherds — how many they kill on my orders, and how many they kill on their own initiative. Record against each shepherd every act of destruction he commits.

**63** Then read back to me by count how many they destroy and how many they hand over for destruction. I want this as testimony against them — to know exactly what every shepherd has done, whether they kept my orders or not.

**64** But don't tell them this. Don't warn them. Just write down every individual act of destruction and document it all."

**65** I watched the shepherds pasture the sheep through their assigned seasons. They began killing far more than they had been authorized, abandoning the sheep to the lions.

**66** The lions and tigers devoured most of the sheep; the wild boars joined in. They burned the tower and demolished the house [the destruction of the First Temple].

**67** I was devastated to see that tower destroyed — the house of the sheep laid waste. After that I could no longer see the sheep going back into the house.

**68** The shepherds and their allies handed the sheep over to all the wild beasts for consumption. Each shepherd received a specified number to destroy. The other [the recording angel] wrote in his book how many each one had killed.

**69** And every one of them killed and destroyed far more than their quota. I began to weep and mourn for those sheep.

**70** I watched in the vision as the one who wrote recorded every sheep destroyed by those shepherds, day by day — then carried the whole book up and laid it before the Lord of the sheep, showing him everything the shepherds had done, all they had taken away, all they had handed over for destruction.

**71** The book was read before the Lord of the sheep. He took it, read it, sealed it, and set it aside.

**72** I then watched the shepherds pasture for twelve hours [the period of the exile]. Then three of those sheep turned back and started rebuilding what had fallen down of the house [the Return from exile; Zerubbabel, Ezra, Nehemiah]. The wild boars tried to stop them but could not.

**73** They rebuilt as before and raised up the tower, which was called the high tower [Zerubbabel's Temple/Second Temple]. They began again to place the table of offering before the tower — but all the bread on it was polluted and impure [the defilement of the Second Temple's worship].

**74** The sheep's eyes remained blinded throughout all this — they did not see clearly. Neither did their shepherds'. Many sheep were handed over for destruction; they were trampled and devoured.

**75** The Lord of the sheep held back until all the sheep were scattered across the field and mingled with the enemy. The shepherds did not rescue them from the beasts.

**76** The one who wrote the book carried it up and read it aloud before the Lord of the sheep's dwelling, pleading for the sheep, presenting all the deeds of the shepherds as testimony against them.

**77** And the Lord of the sheep arose and came to them in wrath. All who saw him fled; they all collapsed into his shadow before his face.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering. Chapter 89 is the longest and most historically rich chapter of the Animal Apocalypse. SYMBOLISM (in order): Noah = white bull become man (v. 1); the Flood (vv. 2-8); Noah's sons: Shem = white, Japheth = red, Ham = black (v. 9); Abraham = white bull (v. 10); Ishmael = wild ass (v. 11); Isaac = white bull (v. 11); Jacob = white sheep (v. 12); twelve tribes = twelve sheep (v. 12); Joseph sold = sheep given to asses then wolves (v. 13); Israel in Egypt = sheep among wolves (v. 14); Moses = sheep who becomes man (vv. 16, 28-38); Exodus = wolves driven back, sea divided (vv. 19-27); Sinai = Moses on the rock (vv. 29-35); Tabernacle = house built by Moses (v. 36); Joshua/Caleb = two new leaders after Jordan (v. 39); Judges period = cycles of blindness (v. 41); Saul = ram who abandons glory (v. 44); David = second ram (v. 45-48); Solomon's Temple = great house with tower (v. 50); the Prophets = sheep sent to warn and killed (v. 51-53); Exile to Babylon = handed to lions (v. 55-59); seventy angelic shepherds = rulers of the nations over exilic Israel (v. 60); First Temple destroyed (v. 66); Second Temple built but polluted (v. 72-73).*
